messages.content: Joseph wants to go to Boston for a road trip. If he takes route A, it will take him 5 hours to arrive; but if he takes route B, it will only take him 2 hours to arrive at his destination. How much time will he save if he takes route B to Boston and back to his home?

To determine how much time Joseph will save by taking route B to Boston and back, we need to compare the total travel time for both routes.

1. **Route A:**
   - One-way travel time: 5 hours
   - Round trip travel time: \(5 \text{ hours} \times 2 = 10 \text{ hours}\)

2. **Route B:**
   - One-way travel time: 2 hours
   - Round trip travel time: \(2 \text{ hours} \times 2 = 4 \text{ hours}\)

3. **Time saved:**
   - Time saved by taking route B: \(10 \text{ hours} - 4 \text{ hours} = 6 \text{ hours}\)

Thus, Joseph will save 6 hours by taking route B to Boston and back.

FINAL: 6
